title: Sheafification of a presheaf of modules has the sheafification of the underlying presheaf of sets
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $\operatorname{Opens}(X)$ be the category whose objects are the open subsets of $X$ and whose morphisms are inclusions; equip it with the opens-site topology in which a family $\{U_j\subseteq U\}_j$ covers $U$ exactly when $U=\bigcup_jU_j$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $\mathcal O_X$ be a sheaf of rings on this site and let $\mathcal P$ be a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Let $\eta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^\#$ be the sheafification of $\mathcal P$ as a presheaf of modules, with its universal property among sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Write $|\mathcal P|$ for the underlying presheaf of sets and $|\mathcal P^\#|$ for the underlying sheaf of sets [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $|\mathcal P^\#|$ with $|\eta|:|\mathcal P|\to|\mathcal P^\#|$ is the sheafification of $|\mathcal P|$: for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal H$ on $\operatorname{Opens}(X)$, composition with $|\eta|$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{PSh}(\operatorname{Opens}(X),\mathrm{Set})}(|\mathcal P^\#|,\mathcal H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{PSh}(\operatorname{Opens}(X),\mathrm{Set})}(|\mathcal P|,\mathcal H)$, where the left-hand morphisms have sheaf source and target.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), together with Sheaves, Lemma 0087 (lemma-sheafify-presheaf-structures), item (1): the module sheafification is the sheafification of the underlying presheaf of abelian groups and hence of sets

mathlib_match.how: For the opens site `J` of `X`, line 79 identifies module sheafification after forgetting modules with additive-group sheafification. Line 233 gives `sheafifyComposeIso` for a value functor preserving sheafification; the concrete forgetful-functor instance is supplied by the hypotheses and instance at lines 305-312. Its compatibility equation at lines 239-241 identifies the unit with the underlying sheafification map, and the module `sheafificationAdjunction` supplies the universal property, so the resulting isomorphism is exactly the sheafification universal property for underlying sets.
